prerequisites: It is recommended not to take this subject until having achieved the most complete possible vision of the technical disciplines taught in the degree.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the requirements and legal and ethical implications of professional engineering practice, particularly in project development.
Know the characteristics of projects, their life cycle, and the technical, economic, safety, environmental, legal, social, and ethical conditions to consider.
Define the scope of a project and plan the deadlines and costs of all necessary tasks, and control progress and supervise the work, keeping the initial plan in mind.
Clearly present and adequately justify the solutions adopted in a project, preparing the associated documents for its contracting and execution.
Understand the structure and functions of a technical office, as well as develop and improve a working method.

syllabus_topics: Theme 6: Regulatory Scope and Project Processing.
teaching_methods: Classroom practices (problem solving and case studies)
Computer lab practices (planning, budgeting, graphic and document management tools)

assessment_methods.method: Theoretical exam (written test with theoretical questions, problems, or case studies)
Laboratory practices (attendance, uploaded exercises, and lab practice exam)

assessment_rules: To pass, a minimum of 5 out of 10 points must be obtained in each of the three parts (theoretical exam, non-classroom work, and laboratory practices). If these minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as 0.4 * Theoretical exam + 0.35 * Non-classroom work + 0.25 * Laboratory practices. Otherwise, the grade will be the minimum between the calculated formula result and 4.0. In the extraordinary call, grades above 5 from the ordinary call can be carried over. For differentiated evaluation, attendance to practices is not mandatory, and the EV-3 calculation varies for the ordinary call (0.25 * submitted exercises + 0.75 * Lab Practice Exam) and the extraordinary call (Lab Practice Exam only).
